title: Jupyter delayed reply and duplicate retry

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: A timeout after request submission means the outcome is unknown; retrying a non-idempotent execution can duplicate work.
hypothesis: The fake transport should mark a request as submitted, report outcome_unknown before the delayed reply, and demonstrate that a blind retry creates a second request.
minimal_fixture: A deterministic fake request table and timer; no real kernel is launched.
predicted_behavior: Before the delayed reply arrives the only honest state is outcome_unknown. A retry increments submitted request count.
observed_behavior: first=1 retry=2 reply=2 requests=((:id 1 :code "counter += 1" :state replied) (:id 2 :code "counter += 1" :state replied))

independent_checks.name: blind retry created a second request

counterexample: Treating timeout as not-run can submit a training cell twice.
derived_gym_requirement: Jupyter actions need request ids, parent headers or equivalent handles, kernel incarnation, and an outcome_unknown state that blocks blind retry of non-idempotent code.
